      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Until recently, the common type of <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span> in children and teens was type 1. It was called juvenile <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span>. With Type 1 <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span>, the pancreas does not make insulin. Insulin is a hormone that helps glucose,or sugar, get into your cells to give them energy. Without insulin, too much sugar stays in the blood.</p><p>Now younger people are also getting type 2 <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span>.  Type 2 <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span> used to be called <span class="qt3">adult-onset</span> <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span>. But now it is becoming more common in children and teens, due to more obesity. With Type 2 <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span>, the body does not make or use insulin well.</p><p>Children have a higher risk of type 2 <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span> if they  are overweight or have obesity, have a family history of <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span>, or are not active. Children who are African American, Hispanic, Native American/Alaska Native, Asian American, or Pacific Islander also have a higher risk. To lower the risk of type 2 <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span> in children:</p><ul><li>Have them maintain a healthy weight</li><li>Be sure they are physically active</li><li>Have them eat smaller portions of healthy foods</li><li>Limit time with the TV, computer, and video</li></ul><p>Children and teens with type 1 <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span> may need to take insulin. Type 2 <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span> may be  controlled with diet and exercise. If not, patients will need to take oral <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span> medicines or insulin. A blood test called the A1C can check on how you are managing your <span class="qt0"><span class="qt2">diabetes</span></span>.</p></content>
